identification: Lobera 0.2.0, Active Directory and network penetration-testing CLI
judgment: Transparent, operator-controlled offensive assessment suite whose implemented actions agree with its declared purpose. No evidence of package trojanization, hidden activation, fixed theft destination, or an undisclosed payload was found in execution-path review. The dangerous capabilities remain accurately detected. The supplied VT flags and classifier are understandable for these payloads but do not establish malicious deployment.
missing_context: Who installed/invoked it, whether the machine is an assessment host, the selected targets, and target-owner authorization are unknown. This verdict is about the reviewed package, not authorization for any deployment.
provenance: forager --all-wheels retrieved the original PyPI lobera@0.2.0 wheel. SHA-256 is identical. Artifacts and .forage.json files remain under scratch/lobera-registry and scratch/lobera-controls. Registry identity corroborates packaging/purpose, not trustworthiness.

execution_paths.behavior: Import exposes main; main initializes local session DB/authentication. Normal protocol invocation lists scripts. --script, --script-fam, or --scanner explicitly selects execution with supplied target/credentials. Fixed local module dispatch is used, not remote module retrieval.

An explicitly selected FTP autopwn scanner can automatically chain webshell upload; has_anon condition currently always returns True and the script performs its own checks. Not every exploit requires a separate per-module confirmation. Normal package import does not enter this path.

Logs into target FTP anonymously; tests writing/deleting a probe; checks web ports; uploads actual request-to-command PHP and ASP payloads. This is real attack capability rather than an inert test fixture.

Authenticates to selected SQL Server. enable_xp_cmdshell sends configuration queries; xp_cmdshell executes chosen command. clr_exec prints a commented external-DLL workflow only. The unsafe assembly/TRUSTWORTHY observations are retained as statements.

Takes realm, SID and krbtgt hash; attempts PAC construction, privileged groups, long-lived EncTicketPart encryption and local ccache output; sets KRB5CCNAME only if forging returns. This is a ticket-forging attempt. PAC data/checksums are incomplete and seq_set calls omit the required name argument in declared Impacket 0.12.0; usable forged tickets are not established.

Checks SMB signing and ADCS endpoint accessibility, assembles relay commands and prints follow-up instructions. Does not itself invoke ntlmrelayx. Directory-service modules separately implement real RBCD and KeyCredentialLink modifications.

Parse operator hash material and call SMBConnection.login with empty password and raw NT hash. The latter three gate this branch on a nonempty nt_hash. Supported suspicious PTH detection added independently of the documentation phrase.

Explicit action dispatch sends PowerShell snippets to authenticated WinRM. ETW payload reflects PSEtwLogProvider.m_enabled and writes zero. Reverse shell is plain TCP despite a comment calling it encrypted; commands received from socket are evaluated with iex and results written back. Endpoint is operator-provided; no hardcoded live C2 endpoint.

SQL-delay and Log4Shell probes and HTTP desync byte sequences are constructed and sent to selected targets. Octal loopback is an SSRF test value. Callbacks default to reserved example.com or user input.

execution_paths.path: core/session_db.py, core/hooks.py and encoding call sites
execution_paths.behavior: Results, credentials and hashes go to local ~/.lobera/session.db. Optional hooks invoke local cracker/exploit tools based on flags. Base64 is used for generated PowerShell commands, file transport and JWT processing; GPP decryption and Kerberos crypto serve disclosed credential-testing features. No opaque install-time encoded payload was found.
